rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act rent cap
rules.requirement: Owners may not raise rent more than 5% plus the local CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, in any 12-month period, and no more than twice in that period. New tenancies may start at any rent. Exempt: affordable/deed-restricted housing, dormitories, housing under stricter local rent control, housing with a certificate of occupancy within the past 15 years, certain separately alienable properties, and owner-occupied duplexes.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower
rules.effective_date_note: Cap first applied to increases on or after 2019-03-15 (text refers to rent as of 2020-01-01); current version (SB 567) effective 2024-01-01, operative 2024-04-01. Mobilehome increases from 2021-02-18.
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted/subsidized affordable housing; dormitories; housing under stricter local rent control; CO within previous 15 years; separately alienable property not owned by REIT/corporation/corporate-member LLC with notice; owner-occupied duplex.
rules.penalty: Civil action for injunctive relief, overcharge damages (up to 3x if willful), attorney's fees; AG, city attorney or county counsel may enforce.
rules.interaction: Does not apply to housing under local rent control that restricts increases to less than the state cap; does not expand or limit local authority under Civ. Code ch. 2.7.

unverifiable_exemptions: single-family homes and condos not owned by REIT, corporation or corporate-member LLC (with notice)

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act – just cause eviction and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: After a tenant has lived in a unit for 12 months, the owner can end the tenancy only for a stated at-fault or no-fault just cause. For no-fault reasons the owner must pay one month's rent in relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent, and the notice must say so.
rules.key_value: Just cause after 12 months; no-fault relocation = 1 month's rent
rules.quoted_span: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy
rules.effective_date_note: Original Tenant Protection Act date (not stated in the section text; text references leases from 2020-01-01/2020-07-01). Current version operative 2024-04-01; AB 1529 amendment effective 2026-01-01.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenant must have occupied 12 months (24 months if adult tenants added).
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels; nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities; dormitories; owner shares bath/kitchen; owner-occupied single-family and duplex; CO within previous 15 years; separately alienable property of non-corporate owner with notice; deed-restricted affordable housing.
rules.penalty: Noncompliant notice void; actual damages, attorney's fees, up to 3x if willful; AG/city attorney/county counsel may seek injunction.
rules.interaction: Does not apply where an earlier (on or before 9/1/2019) or more protective local just-cause ordinance applies.

unverifiable_exemptions: separately alienable homes/condos of non-corporate owners with notice
dormitories, hospitals, care facilities, transient hotels

rules.title: California residential security deposit limits and return rules
rules.requirement: Landlords may not demand or receive security over one month's rent (two months for qualifying small landlords with no more than two properties and four units, except for service members), in addition to first month's rent. Deposit must be held for the tenant, photos taken, and the deposit returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after the tenant vacates.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords)
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy
rules.effective_date_note: Cap applies to security collected on or after 2024-07-01 (AB 12, subd. (c)(6)); current text amended by AB 414 effective 2026-01-01.
rules.coverage_conditions: Security for rental agreement of residential property used as tenant's dwelling.
rules.exemptions: Two-month cap for natural-person/all-natural-person LLC landlords owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units total; not for service-member tenants.
rules.penalty: Bad-faith retention: statutory damages up to twice the deposit plus actual damages.

coverage.landlord_size_condition: Two-month cap only for natural person/LLC of natural persons owning no more than 2 properties with no more than 4 units total
unverifiable_exemptions: small landlord status for two-month cap

rules.title: California application screening fee limits
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge a screening fee only up to actual out-of-pocket costs and time, capped at $30 per applicant adjusted annually for CPI since 1998. No fee if no unit is or will soon be available; landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, give a copy of the credit report within 7 days, and offer first-come screening or a full refund to unselected applicants.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted since 1998 (Berkeley Rent Board cites $68.96 for 2026)
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant
rules.effective_date_note: Date of the current AB 1170 amendment; the $30 CPI-adjusted cap itself dates from earlier versions (CPI adjustment from 1998).
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords (owners of residential rental property) and agents charging applicants, including guarantors/cosigners.
rules.interaction: Fee is not 'security' under § 1950.5; does not preempt federal/state housing assistance program rules.
rules.conflict_note: The statute states $30 adjusted by CPI but no single current dollar figure; Berkeley Rent Board page (D005) states $68.96 for 2026 and is not an official statewide figure.

rules.title: FEHA source-of-income protections (incl. Section 8, HUD-VASH, credit-history limit for subsidy holders)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate against or harass applicants or tenants based on source of income, including Section 8 and HUD-VASH vouchers, and 'No Section 8' policies are unlawful. For tenants with a government rent subsidy, income standards must be based on the tenant's portion of rent and applicants must be allowed to offer alternative evidence instead of credit history. Asking about level or source of income is still allowed.
rules.key_value: Ban on source-of-income discrimination incl. Section 8 and HUD-VASH vouchers
rules.quoted_span: For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person
rules.effective_date_note: Per D015, SB 329 made government subsidies 'source of income' as of 2020-01-01; SB 267 amendment (credit-history and HUD-VASH provisions) effective 2024-01-01.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied home renting to one additional person

rules.title: California Civil Rights Council criminal-history housing regulations
rules.requirement: Landlords may check criminal history but blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record are prohibited, as are policies that consider arrests without convictions. Denials based on a conviction must be directly related to being a good tenant or to safety.
rules.key_value: No blanket criminal-record bans; no use of arrests without convictions
rules.citation: California Civil Rights Council housing criminal history regulations (FEHA regulations)
citation_aliases: Civil Rights Council criminal history regulations
rules.quoted_span: Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record are prohibited, as are policies that consider arrests without convictions
rules.effective_date_note: D015 says the regulations took effect Jan. 1, 2020.
rules.review_note: The documents do not give the regulation section number; none cited. D016 (CRD) confirms the same limits.

rules.title: AB 325 – Common pricing algorithm prohibition (Cartwright Act)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to influence prices) as part of a conspiracy to restrain trade, or to use or distribute one while coercing others to adopt its recommended prices or terms. Single-firm algorithms using only the business's own data are not covered.
rules.key_value: Ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data in restraint of trade or with coercion
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.effective_date_note: Chaptered 2025-10-06; D028 states the laws took effect January 1, 2026 (D022 itself gives no effective date).
rules.penalty: Cartwright Act penalties; per D028 criminal fines up to $6M (corporations)/$1M (individuals) or twice gain/loss, civil fines up to $1M in AG/DA actions, treble damages and fees in private suits.
rules.interaction: Does not impair other antitrust laws; not limited to housing.

parsed.notes: Consolidated CA state records: the duplicate §1950.5, §1950.6, Gov. Code §12955 and AB 325 candidates are merged. The criminal-history regulations are kept separate and cited by name because the documents give no section number. No link-only sources were needed.
